h: The Census That Renews the Souls of Yisrael

p: וַיְדַבֵּר ה׳ אֶל מֹשֶׁה בְּמִדְבַּר סִינַי
"And Hashem spoke to Moshe in the Wilderness of Sinai,
בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (בְּמִדְבַּר רַבָּה א, ז)
In the Midrash Rabbah on this parsha (Bamidbar Rabbah 1:7):
With three things the Torah was given:
with fire, with water and with the wilderness, etc.
And why was the Torah given
כָּל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹשֶׂה עַצְמוֹ הֶפְקֵר כַּמִּדְבָּר
whoever does not make himself ownerless like the wilderness
cannot acquire the wisdom and the Torah."
Now the matter of fire and water,
with which the Torah was given,
אֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם שַׁיָּיכוּת לְפָרָשָׁה זוֹ
has no connection at all to this parsha;
because "in the Wilderness of Sinai" is mentioned here,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם טְפֵי הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְהַמִּדְרָשׁ
it would nevertheless have been more fitting for the Midrash
to place its exposition in Parshas Yisro,
at the time of Mattan Torah,
בַּיּוֹם הַזֶּה בָּאוּ מִדְבַּר סִינָי (שְׁמוֹת יט, א)
"On this day they came to the Wilderness of Sinai" (Shemos 19:1).
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב
But the matter is according to what is written
בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (קיז, א)
in the holy Zohar at the beginning of this parsha (Zohar III 117a)
עַל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּמִדְבַּר סִינַי בְּאוֹהֶל מוֹעֵד
on what is said, "in the Wilderness of Sinai, in the Tent of Meeting":
"Once the Torah and the Mishkan had been established,
to count the hosts of the Torah:
how many hosts belong to the Torah
and how many hosts belong to the Mishkan."
And this follows what is written
(in the Mishnah at the end of Taanis, 26b)
"'With the crown with which his mother crowned him' etc.
'On the day of his wedding' — this is Mattan Torah;
'and on the day of the joy of his heart'
this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash,
may it be rebuilt speedily in our days."
That is, "with the crown with which his mother crowned him":
these are the two crowns of Na'aseh and Nishma.
For at the time of Mattan Torah
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּדְרָשׁ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ג, יא)
as it is expounded in the Midrash (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 3:11):
מַהוּ בָּעֲטָרָה שֶׁעִטְּרָה לּוֹ אִמּוֹ כּוּלֵּי
"What is 'with the crown with which his mother crowned him'? etc.
He did not cease cherishing them
That is, "his mother" is Knesses Yisrael.
וְאָז עִטֵּר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
And then HaKadosh Baruch Hu crowned Yisrael
אִיתָא בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (יִתְרוֹ סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה כז)
it is stated in the Midrash Rabbah (Shemos Rabbah 27:9, end of the chapter, on Yisro):
And with the building of the Beis HaMikdash
וְזֶהוּ בְּיוֹם חֲתוּנָּתוֹ זֶה מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
And this is "on the day of his wedding — this is Mattan Torah":
"and on the day of the joy of his heart
this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash":
this is the crown of Na'aseh,
for there is the essence and root of the place of the avodah.
And this is "how many hosts belong to the Torah":
יֵשׁ לוֹ שׁוֹרֶשׁ בְּאוֹת מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
has a root in a letter of the words of Torah,
as is written in the holy sefarim:
six hundred thousand letters for the Torah,
and this is alluded to in the initials of the word Yisrael, as is known.
And although the count is not exact,
Alef, Yud, Vav, Yud and the like;
and the root of the soul of every one of Yisrael
אוֹת אוֹ חֵלֶק מֵאוֹת בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
is a letter or part of a letter in the words of Torah;
and this is "the hosts of the Torah."
means that every one of Yisrael
has the resting of the Shechinah in his heart,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא פִּנְחָס רל, א)
as is written (Ra'aya Mehemna, Pinchas, Zohar III 230a):
for when a person pictures in his heart
שֶׁמֶּלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
that the King of the kings of kings, HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
stands over him and sees his deeds,
the fear of Heaven will immediately come to him
(Hagahah at the beginning of Orach Chaim, 1:1);
and this corresponds to the crown of Na'aseh.
we call her Torah she'b'al peh"
בָּא רַק עַל יְדֵי עָמָל וִיגִיעָה
comes only through toil and exertion,
that a person does not merit it
all the matters of this world;
for there is great suffering in it
and the wandering of sleep, etc.
And on this the Midrash brought here
the pasuk "in the Tent of Meeting,"
when Torah she'b'al peh became necessary
"For in much wisdom is much anger"
and on this they expounded "in the wilderness" here:
that a person does not merit that words of Torah
שֶׁהָיָה עַל יְדֵי נְתִינַת לוּחוֹת שְׁנִיּוֹת
that came about through the giving of the second Luchos,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (תִּשָּׂא פָּרָשָׁה מו)
as they said in the Midrash Rabbah (Shemos Rabbah 46:1, Ki Sisa)
רַק מִי שֶׁמֵּשִׂים עַצְמוֹ הֶפְקֵר כַּמִּדְבָּר
only one who makes himself ownerless like the wilderness.
"And they declared their pedigrees according to their families" (Bamidbar 1:18),
to bring the record of their lineage.
And the Ramban raised a difficulty on this;
that they were born and became a new creation,
in which they mentioned their names and the names of their fathers
and Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, and the Nesi'im,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לִנְפָשׁוֹת חֲדָשׁוֹת
through this they merited new souls.
And this is "the hosts of the Torah
and the hosts of the Mishkan."

p: And on Shabbos as well there is
"the day of his wedding — this is Mattan Torah,"
that all agree the Torah was given on Shabbos.
for Shabbos corresponds to the middah of Malchus,
we call her Torah she'b'al peh."
And so it is stated explicitly in the holy Zohar
בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי דָּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
"'On the seventh day' — this is Torah she'b'al peh,
for through it the world was perfected."
And likewise on Shabbos there is
"the day of the joy of his heart
this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash";
for on Shabbos every one of Yisrael
is a dwelling for the Shechinah,
as is written in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 48):
זַכָּאָה מַאן דְּעָבִיד לוֹן דִּירָה בְּשַׁבָּת
fortunate is he who makes them a dwelling on Shabbos
in the two chambers of the heart."
is like the Mikdash in the world.
וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ גַּם כֵּן שְׁתֵּי הָעֲטָרוֹת
And it too has the two crowns,
And this is "the hosts of the Torah
and the hosts of the Mishkan."
And this Chumash is called "Chumash HaPekudim,"
"and 'On the tenth' that is in Chumash HaPekudim";
for the holiness of this Chumash
is the matter of the countings.
For each of the five Chumshei Torah
corresponding to the five Chumshei Torah."
And the holiness of this Chumash
הוּא מַה שֶּׁזָּכוּ עַל יְדֵי הַפְּקוּדִים
is what they merited through the countings,
שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד הִזְכִּיר שְׁמוֹ וְשֵׁם אָבִיו
in which each one mentioned his name and his father's name
לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְלִפְנֵי מֹשֶׁה
before HaKadosh Baruch Hu and before Moshe,
and from this they merited a new neshamah,
as it says, "And they declared their pedigrees according to their families,"
the counting of those who entered the Land.
And on this they said in Bereishis Rabbah
וַיַּבְדֵּל אֱלֹהִים בֵּין הָאוֹר וּבֵין הַחוֹשֶׁךְ (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, ד)
"And God separated between the light and the darkness" (Bereishis 1:4),
between those who left Mitzrayim and those who entered the Land.
And as has been explained elsewhere,
this is the matter of Torah she'bichsav
as is written in the Tanchuma that we mentioned.
